name: Index page
markup: No html in this file. Each variant below carries the path to its own markup at r/index-page/<variant>.html — fetch the one you need.
description: The register screen as a whole page: the breadcrumb and the one h1, the saved views, the filter band, the toolbar that becomes a selection toolbar, the table, the pager, and the states the page as a whole can be in.
when_to_use: The front door of a module, as a whole page — the purchase order register, the GRN register, the indent queue, the vendor list, a ledger. The line that decides most screens is the one against data-table, and it is the line between a region and a page. data-table is the panel: one array of records with a search box, sortable headers, column visibility, selection, totals and a pager, all inside a single bordered card, and it is what you drop into a tab, a dialog, a dashboard column or the body of this layout. This entry is everything around that panel — the trail and the one h1, the count line that answers what the page is showing, the saved views a buyer opens every morning, the filter band in the header and what it becomes below sm, where the primary action lives and why it does not move, the status tabs over the top, the selection toolbar that takes the band over, and the two different nothings a register can be in. Reach for data-table when the register is one region of a screen that has other regions; reach for this when the register is the screen — and then the panel inside it is data-table's markup with its toolbar dropped, because this page has already taken the search and the filters up into the header band and two search boxes on one screen is how a PO number gets typed into the wrong one. Against list-detail: that is a queue worked one record at a time, keyboard-driven, the queue never leaving the screen, and the test is whether the next record matters. On a register it does not — a register is scanned, sorted, filtered and acted on in bulk, and it wants the whole width for the columns being compared rather than a third of it for a queue nobody is walking. Against table: that is rows and a sortable header and nothing else, no page around them, and it is what both this and data-table are built out of. A screen that creates or edits one of these records is form-page.
rules: This is a composition and not a new register. The panel in every variant is data-table's markup — the same sortable header button, the same chevron, the same status pill, the same select-all bound with x-effect, the same range-and-total footer — and the page's own contribution is what sits around it: which regions exist, in what order, what the band does when a selection appears, and which states the whole screen can be in.

When the page carries the filter band, the panel drops its toolbar. data-table puts search and filters inside the panel because the panel is the whole component; a page puts them in the header band because they also drive the count under the h1, the saved view, the tab counts and the export. Keep both and the screen has two search boxes over one list, and the one somebody types into is the one they happen to be nearest.

One h1 and it is the page's, and it survives every state — the selection toolbar, the empty register, the first paint. The band gives up the trail, the count line, the filter row and the action cluster when a selection takes it over, and it keeps the h1, because a heading outline that loses its top-level heading when five rows are ticked is a document that changes its title while you are reading it.

The primary action lives in the header band and does not move between states. It is the page's action, not an answer to what the list currently shows, so it is in the same corner on a full register, a filtered one and an empty one. The empty block underneath never repeats it as a second filled button — it offers the bordered alternative and a link, and the fill stays where it always is.

The empty block under a filter offers no create at all. That is data-table's rule and it survives at page level with one clarification worth writing down, because the two look like a contradiction: the header band's primary stays, because it is the page's action and it is there on every state of the screen, while the block in the middle of an empty result offers only ways back out of the query. A create button drawn as the answer to "nothing matched" is how the same order gets raised twice.

A register nobody has used and a register whose query matched nothing are different screens and must not look the same. The first has no toolbar, no header row and no pager — every one of them is chrome describing an absence — and it says something factual about why it is empty, a commissioning date or an opening balance. The second keeps the filter band and the chips, because the query is the thing that has to be undone, and it names what is in force.

Below sm the whole filter band is a drawer, and the count of what is in force goes on its trigger. Five selects stacked on a phone is a screen of chrome above the first row, and a phone that hides the filters without saying how many are on is a register that looks wrong and cannot be diagnosed. The chips stay on screen at every width — they are the answer to what is applied, and they are the one thing that must not go into the drawer with the controls.

Both copies of a filter — the row at sm and up, the drawer below it — bind to the same state and are both in the DOM, with the inactive one display:none so it is out of the tab order as well as off the screen. Two independent copies drift the moment somebody rotates a tablet.

Saved views are the page's memory and they are not tabs. Each one is a stored query somebody named, one is current, and the moment a filter moves off the saved definition the page has to say so and offer three answers — save into this view, save as a new one, reset. Keep the changed filters silently under the saved name and tomorrow morning "My open POs" is not what was saved, and nobody can tell whether the view or the data changed.

Status tabs over a register are a filter wearing a tab shape, so there is one panel and it is relabelled rather than five panels holding five copies of the same table. Switching a tab returns to page one and changes the total, and the counts on the tabs are the same query with the status predicate removed — they narrow when the search or the filters narrow, or the tab labelled 34 opens onto 6 rows and the number becomes something nobody trusts.

The count line under the h1 is a role="status" in the document from first paint, and it is where the page answers "what am I looking at". Filters, tabs and search all write to it. A second live region on the panel talks over it.

Density and column choice belong to the person, not to the visit. They are the two settings a buyer who is on this screen all day changes once, so they are persisted per user and the page comes back the way it was left; a register that resets to comfortable on every navigation is one somebody sets four times a day and then stops setting.

The snippet root is a bounded scroller — h-[640px], rounded-xl, border-zinc-300 — so a whole screen previews in a box, and the filter drawer is absolute inset-0 against that frame. As a real page it renders inside app-shell's <main>: drop the wrapper's height and border, keep the mx-auto max-w-[1600px] gutter on the band and on the body so the h1 and the panel line up, let the sticky band stick to the shell's scrolling column, and make the drawer fixed inset-0.

anatomy.description: page-header's <header> inside <main>: white, edge to edge across the column, over a border-zinc-200 rule, its content in the same mx-auto max-w-[1600px] gutter the body uses. Never overflow-hidden — the column menu and the view menu open out of it.
The breadcrumb above the title, from breadcrumbs, present here only if the topbar does not carry one. Two crumbs on a top-level register is ceremony; a module root has none at all.

The one h1, and under it a role="status" line saying what the page is showing — how many of how many, and what they are worth. Figures take tabular-nums so the band does not reflow as a filter narrows.
A <nav> of named queries under the title, one carrying aria-current, plus the strip that appears when the current view has been filtered away from.
The second row inside the band: page-header's filter row — a <form role="search">, the narrow selects, and below sm a Filters trigger carrying the active count.
One removable chip per filter in force, with Clear all as a link beside them. Visible at every width, including when the controls have gone into the drawer.
Optional, joined to the band's bottom edge with -mb-px. A filter in a tab shape: one register panel below, relabelled as the selection moves.

What the band becomes when rows are ticked: the same h1 element, a tinted count pill beside it, the scope written into the count line's own role="status", the actions that apply and the way out. The trail, the action cluster and the filter row give way to it.
data-table's panel with its toolbar dropped — the sortable header, the rows, the card list below md, and the footer. Rounded, bordered, on the page ground.
pagination's footer inside the panel: the range, the total and the page position, ends disabled rather than removed so the control keeps its width.
What fills the panel when the count is zero, in one of two shapes that must not be confused — nothing ever raised here, or nothing matching this query.
Below sm, drawer's bottom sheet holding the same controls the row holds at sm and up, with Reset and a button naming the count it would show.

behaviour: The filter band narrows the list underneath and never navigates. Every control applies on change, the chips rebuild, the count line under the h1 rewrites, and the pager returns to page one — page 4 of a two-row result shows nothing.
The primary action is in the same place on every state of the page. Nothing about the list moves it, hides it or promotes a second filled button beside it.

Selecting rows swaps the band's trail, action cluster and filter row for the selection toolbar in place, keeps the same h1 element, and rewrites the count line rather than adding a second one. Nothing stacks below the band and no row under it moves down.

The selection is an array of record ids on the page root, so it survives sorting, filtering and paging, and the toolbar states the scope as well as the size. Pressing Next is guarded rather than disabled, so the button keeps focus and the count is still there when the new page lands.
Ticking every row on the page is not selecting the query. Selecting everything that matches is a second, deliberate act with its own count, and touching any row afterwards drops the claim.
Switching a status tab returns to page one, changes the total in the footer and rewrites the count line. The trail, the h1 and the actions do not change, because it is the same register either way.

A saved view sets every filter at once. While the current filters differ from the saved ones the view reads as modified and the strip offers save, save-as and reset; picking another view discards the difference the same way Reset does.

Below sm the filter controls move into a drawer whose trigger carries the number in force, and the chips stay on the page. The drawer closes on Escape and on its own Show button, and focus returns to the trigger.
Density and the column set change the rows in place without a fetch. Hiding a column drops its header, its cells and the same field from the card layout below md.

Nothing on this page scrolls sideways at 390px. The table restacks into cards, the filter row becomes a drawer, and the only region allowed to scroll horizontally is the status tab row, because a second line of tabs reads as a different control.
accessibility: One <main>, one <h1>, and the band is a <header> inside <main> rather than the banner landmark — the banner belongs to the topbar. Regions below the h1 are h2.

The count line is a role="status" rendered with the page, so a filter, a tab or a search writes a change into a region that was already there. A live region that arrives with its message already in it is announced to nobody.
The filter band is a <form role="search"> holding a labelled input, and each chip's remove button names the filter it drops — "Remove the filter Overdue", never "Remove".

Saved views are a <nav> with its own name and the current one carries aria-current="true". They are not a tablist, because there are no panels to switch, and not a radiogroup, because each view is somewhere you go and every one of them should be reachable with Tab rather than behind an arrow-key contract.

The status tabs are the tabs component in full — role="tablist" with a name, aria-selected, aria-controls, roving tabindex, arrow, Home and End all preventing default — over a single role="tabpanel" whose aria-labelledby is bound to the selected tab. One panel, relabelled, because all five tabs draw the same table of a different subset.
Sortable headers are buttons inside <th scope="col"> and the <th> carries aria-sort. The chevron is decoration; aria-sort is the answer.

Every row checkbox is labelled with its document number and the select-all says how many rows on this page it covers. The select-all is a native box carrying the indeterminate property, which is already mapped to mixed, so nothing writes aria-checked.
The selection toolbar keeps the same h1 element it replaced the rest of the band around, and its count and scope are one role="status" so a page change re-announces what the selection now spans.

A pager button that is guarded rather than disabled still says so: it carries aria-disabled while it is at a limit, so the keyboard user is told the press will do nothing instead of pressing it twice, and it keeps focus and its place in the tab order the way a disabled button cannot.

A register still loading is aria-busy on the panel with one sr-only role="status" naming what is loading, and the grey rows are aria-hidden — otherwise a screen reader walks twenty-five empty cells and is never told why.

The empty block's heading is an h2 under the page's h1, so an empty register still has an outline, and its text says which nothing this is rather than leaving the user to guess between a filter, a permission and a failure.

The filter drawer is a role="dialog" with aria-modal, a focus trap, Escape closing it and focus returning to the trigger it opened from, and the trigger names the count it carries in its own text rather than in a title.
